summary: Model hot-swap reload loop causing repeated upstream crashes and elevated 5xx at API gateway
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 08:50 UTC PolyNova Health reported a sudden spike of 5xx responses for streaming and sync generate endpoints. Impact: ~30% of requests for the tenant returned 502/503/504 over a 40-minute window; customer-facing SLAs degraded. Environment: Dedicated pool (prod-us-west) backing PolyNova tenant. Timeline: 08:48 first elevated 5xx seen on dashboard; 08:55 support ticket opened; 09:10 SRE alerted. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send concurrent streaming requests pinned to opt-redwood-30b-quant-v2 with typical prompt bundle. 2) Observe connection termination and 5xx responses after model swap. Observed behavior: Serving-runtime logs show repeated model unload/load cycles (hot-swap) for the tenant's pinned model. Each reload sequence produces a short period of elevated memory pressure, OOM restarts in a subset of runtime workers, and transient 502s from API gateway. There is an amplification loop: model-manager initiates hot-swap to apply a quantization fallback, runtime fails warms back up, model-manager re-issues hot-swap, repeat. Temporary workaround applied: routing reduced to fallback cpu-path and disabled automatic hot-swap for the tenant at 09:25 UTC which reduced 5xx to <1%.

2026-03-10 09:18 - SRE-Triage (Marco Ruiz): Identified repeating model reload events on dedicated workers. Correlating with model-manager events.
2026-03-10 09:26 - Marco Ruiz: Applied temporary route reduction and disabled hot-swap for customer. Asked model-team to check model-manager policy.
2026-03-10 11:03 - Elena Novak (Model Ops): Confirmed model-manager initiated a fallback quantization pass after telemetry flagged tokenization mismatch; rollback queued for 11:15.

investigation_notes: Pattern: reload-loop originates from model-manager 'hot-swap' job triggered by auto-quantization fallback when runtime reports inconsistent kernel for quantized weights.
Metrics: saw worker RSS spike ~20% before restart; p95 latency for token generation jumped from 220ms to 1.6s during reload windows.
Logs: runtime stderr shows repeated 'KV cache restore failed' followed by 'worker exit: OOM' on three pods (pod ids: rtd-7b-a12, rtd-7b-a13, rtd-30b-b04).
API gateway: upstream health checks mark subset unhealthy for ~30s causing 502 fanout until health restored; connection retries amplified error rate.

Hypothesis: model-manager's fallback path is too aggressive under low-memory conditions on dedicated nodes; repeated attempts to reload a partially corrupted quantized shard trigger worker OOMs and upstream 5xx.
Cross-ref: similar symptom set to SUP-32789 (model fanout backpressure), but root cause here tied to hot-swap retry logic and quantization fallback ordering.
Observed that autoscaler did not add capacity during the loop due to cooldown policy which allowed degradation to persist longer than expected.
mitigation: 2026-03-10 09:25 - Disabled automatic hot-swap for PolyNova tenant via model-manager feature-flag.
2026-03-10 09:30 - Rerouted a portion of traffic to a verified smaller quantized model (rwd-llm-7b-quantized) as a safe fallback.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Temporarily increased dedicated pool capacity by +2 nodes to absorb load while we assess model artifacts.
Advised customer to postpone heavy batch streams until fixed; customer accepted temporary throttling for stability.
next_steps: Model-team to produce patched hot-swap logic that verifies shard integrity before triggering reload (ETA 2026-03-13).
SRE to adjust autoscaler cooldown policy for dedicated pools handling enterprise tenants (investigation ticket INT-4092).
Run a controlled canary of patched model-manager on staging with reproducible harness (PR referenced above), then schedule a production rollout during low-traffic window.
Postmortem to be authored and shared with PolyNova's technical contact once root cause confirmed and fix deployed.
resolution: Triage ongoing; temporary mitigations reduced error rate to acceptable levels. Awaiting model-manager hot-swap fix and autoscaler tuning.
